item.name: Termux gateway foreground tmux lifecycle
item.contract: Gateway lifecycle commands and docs present a Termux-specific foreground/tmux model: Telegram/Discord/Slack gateways are supported from a foreground shell or tmux session, systemd/Windows service assumptions are not advertised, and doctor/status guidance names termux-wake-lock plus Android battery settings as best-effort survival aids. The implementation must preserve the same gateway command names and JSON contracts as desktop Linux.
item.degraded_mode: If Termux lacks tmux or termux-wake-lock, gateway startup remains possible but doctor/status emits WARN guidance. Android process death is treated as recoverable operator environment behavior, not a Gormes crash.
item.fixture: cmd/gormes gateway/doctor fixtures under synthetic Termux env

Gateway command tests can run with temp GORMES_HOME and fake runtime status stores.
Termux install docs identify foreground/tmux as the supported local gateway model.
not_ready_when: The command tries to install systemd units, Android services, or Termux:Boot entries by default.
Doctor/status claims guaranteed unattended background uptime on Android.
Gateway command names, flags, or JSON shapes diverge from desktop Linux only for Termux.
acceptance: Synthetic Termux doctor/status output includes foreground/tmux and wake-lock guidance.
Gateway start/status/stop command surfaces keep the same names and JSON contracts under synthetic Termux env.
Termux docs explain tmux, termux-wake-lock, battery optimization, and Termux:Boot as operator-managed aids.
No test starts live Telegram/Discord/Slack connections or Android services.
done_signal: Gateway fixtures and docs prove Termux uses the same operator CLI with foreground/tmux lifecycle guidance and bounded Android process-survival claims.

item.name: Kernel tool loop
item.contract: The kernel executes Hermes-style multi-round tool_calls through the native Go registry, defaults to the upstream Hermes 90-turn tool iteration budget, and when an explicit budget is exhausted it asks the model for one extra toolless summary instead of surfacing a raw `tool iteration limit exceeded` error to the channel user.
item.degraded_mode: If the summary request cannot be opened or returns no visible content, the kernel finalizes a bounded assistant fallback message rather than emitting a raw PhaseFailed budget error.
ready_when: Native tool registry descriptors and tool-call continuation messages are already available in the kernel.
Hermes max-iteration summary behavior is source-mapped from run_agent.py.
acceptance: TestKernel_ToolCallHandshake_Echo proves tool_call execution and continuation through the native registry.
TestKernel_DefaultToolIterationBudgetMatchesHermesBeyondTen proves the default budget no longer fails at 10 and matches Hermes' 90-turn default.
TestKernel_ToolIterationBudgetRequestsToollessSummary proves budget exhaustion strips tools, appends Hermes' summary request, and finishes as a normal assistant response rather than PhaseFailed.
item.note: 2026-04-30 parity follow-up: the Telegram report showed raw `tool iteration limit exceeded (10)` leaking to the user. Hermes uses a 90-turn default and, on budget exhaustion, appends a no-tools summary request. Gormes now mirrors that path with requestMaxIterationSummary and keeps the turn in the normal assistant-finalization path so gateway channels do not render a red failure bubble for iteration budget exhaustion.
done_signal: Kernel fixtures prove native tool execution, Hermes 90-turn default budget, and toolless summary finalization on budget exhaustion.

item.degraded_mode: Without the delegation surface, Gormes operators cannot hand a coding task to codex/claude-code/opencode from within Gormes and must shell out manually; doctor and tool registry report no coding-agent workers.

item.name: Gateway manual reset session-boundary hooks
item.contract: Gormes ports Hermes' explicit session-boundary hook behavior for channel reset commands: `/new` and `/reset` fire an old-session finalize hook before resetting, then fire a new-session reset hook after the replacement session is established, preserve hook ordering evidence, continue reset success when a hook fails, and keep expiry-finalization hooks separate from manual reset hooks.
item.degraded_mode: Hook failures emit redacted session_boundary_hook_failed evidence and never block the operator-visible reset acknowledgement; missing hooks degrade to no-op without changing session map clearing or active-turn refusal behavior.
ready_when: Gateway hook registry and session expiry hook cleanup retry evidence are complete, so manual reset can reuse the existing in-process hook seam without inventing a second hook engine.
The worker can test with fake channels, fake kernels, fake session maps, and hook recorders only; no Telegram, Slack, Discord, SQLite session database, provider, or Hermes Python runtime is required.
This slice only adds manual reset boundary hook events and evidence; it does not change expiry scanning, cached-agent cleanup, or session key generation.
not_ready_when: The slice changes reset command authorization, active-turn reset refusal, pairing/session key derivation, session expiry retry policy, or kernel ResetSession semantics.
A hook error prevents a successful reset from reaching the operator or leaks full prompt text, channel message text, provider credentials, local paths, or raw hook stdout/stderr.
The implementation merges manual `/new` reset hooks with expiry-finalization hooks so one path can double-fire the other.
blocked_by: Session expiry hook cleanup retry evidence
acceptance: TestGatewayManualResetFiresFinalizeBeforeResetHook proves an EventReset with an existing mapped session fires on_session_finalize for the old session, clears the mapping, then fires on_session_reset for the new session.
TestGatewayManualResetHookErrorDoesNotBlockReset proves a failing finalize or reset hook records redacted evidence and still sends `Session reset. Next message starts fresh.`.
TestGatewayManualResetDuringActiveTurnDoesNotFireHooks proves ErrResetDuringTurn preserves the existing refusal text and fires no boundary hooks.
TestGatewayManualResetHooksStaySeparateFromExpiryHooks proves FinalizeExpiredSessions still uses expiry_finalize evidence only and manual reset does not mark expiry_finalized metadata.
Existing TestManagerHooksReceiveLifecycle and TestManagerHooksSendLifecycle remain green, proving before/after receive/send hook behavior is unchanged.
done_signal: Gateway reset-hook fixtures prove finalize-before-reset ordering, hook-error tolerance, active-turn no-fire behavior, expiry separation, and unchanged receive/send hook lifecycle.

provenance.note: Hermes fires plugin lifecycle hooks around explicit `/new` and `/reset` session boundaries. Gormes already has generic gateway hooks and expiry finalization, but no row covering manual reset finalize/reset hook ordering.

item.name: Gateway session reset notification parity
item.contract: Gormes ports Hermes' automatic session-reset read model and notification policy for channel sessions: idle, daily, and suspended reset decisions carry a stable reason string; replacement sessions record was_auto_reset, auto_reset_reason, and reset_had_activity without being treated as explicit fresh resets; operator notifications respect SessionResetPolicy.notify and notify_exclude_platforms defaults; and API/webhook-style platforms are excluded from unsolicited reset messages.
item.degraded_mode: Expired, suspended, no-activity, notification-disabled, excluded-platform, and notification-send-failed cases return auto_reset_* evidence with session ids, reason, platform, and activity booleans only; message text, prompt content, provider credentials, and raw channel payloads remain redacted.
ready_when: Gateway manual reset session-boundary hooks are planned and the worker can keep explicit reset hooks separate from auto-reset notices.
Session expiry hook cleanup retry evidence is complete, so auto-reset notification evidence can reuse existing session metadata and status seams without changing expiry finalization.

Tests can use fake clocks, fake session metadata, fake channels, and fake notification senders only; no live Telegram, Slack, Discord, API server, webhook, provider, or SQLite production store is required.

The implementation sends notifications to api_server/webhook by default, treats idle/daily auto resets as explicit fresh-reset skill injection, or loses reset_had_activity evidence.
Warnings include raw user message text, prompt/system context, channel payload bodies, provider credentials, or home-directory paths.
blocked_by: Session expiry hook cleanup retry evidence
acceptance: TestGatewayAutoResetReasonDecision proves idle, daily, suspended, and none decisions return stable reason strings without mutating explicit reset state.
TestGatewayAutoResetSessionMetadata proves replacement sessions record was_auto_reset, auto_reset_reason, and reset_had_activity based on prior token/message activity.
TestGatewayAutoResetNotifyPolicyDefaults proves notify defaults true while api_server and webhook are excluded by default.

TestGatewayAutoResetDoesNotLookFresh proves idle/daily auto-reset sessions do not set the explicit fresh-reset flag used by skill injection, matching Hermes' manual-vs-auto boundary.
TestGatewayAutoResetNotificationSendFailureEvidence proves send failures produce redacted evidence and do not block session creation.
done_signal: Auto-reset fixtures prove reason strings, metadata, notify defaults/excludes, manual-vs-auto freshness separation, send-failure evidence, and no live channel/provider dependencies.

provenance.note: Hermes distinguishes automatic idle/daily/suspended resets from explicit `/new` resets and controls channel notifications through SessionResetPolicy. Gormes has config fields and manual reset planning but no source-backed row for auto-reset notification semantics.

item.name: Gateway slash-confirm session-boundary cleanup
item.contract: Gormes ports Hermes' session-boundary cleanup for pending slash-command confirmations: a channel-neutral pending confirmation store can register exactly one confirmable slash action per gateway session, resolve or clear it once, and successful `/new` or `/reset` clears only the target session's pending confirmation without running the action or touching other sessions.
item.degraded_mode: A nil or empty confirmation store is a no-op; reset refusal during an active turn leaves pending confirmations intact; stale, mismatched, or already-resolved confirmations fail closed with typed errors and no handler execution.
ready_when: Gateway manual reset session-boundary hooks and approval queue cleanup semantics are complete, so this slice can add slash-confirm state without changing session key derivation or reset hook ordering.
Tests can use fake channels, fake kernels, and in-memory confirmation queues only; no Telegram, Slack, Discord, provider, MCP server, or Hermes Python runtime is required.
The row is scoped to the confirmation store plus reset-boundary clearing; `/reload-mcp` execution, adapter buttons, text fallback commands, and component authorization remain separate surfaces.
not_ready_when: The implementation turns `/reload-mcp`, `/approve`, `/always`, or `/cancel` into live gateway commands instead of only adding the session-boundary confirmation state primitive.
A reset clears confirmations before kernel ResetSession succeeds or after ErrResetDuringTurn, causing an active session's pending confirmation to disappear without a real boundary switch.
The confirmation store records prompt text, credentials, adapter callback payloads, local paths, or raw channel messages in outcomes or progress evidence.
acceptance: TestSlashConfirmQueueRegisterSupersedesAndClearScoped proves registering a new confirmation supersedes the old one for the same session, preserves other sessions, and scoped clear removes only the target session without recording an approval-like outcome.
TestSlashConfirmQueueResolveOnce validates once/always/cancel choices, ID mismatch fail-closed behavior, and double-resolution protection without invoking stale handlers.

TestManager_ResetClearsSlashConfirmationForTargetSessionOnly proves successful EventReset clears the target session's pending slash confirmation while preserving another session's pending confirmation.
TestManager_ResetDuringActiveTurnPreservesSlashConfirmation proves ErrResetDuringTurn keeps the pending confirmation and existing refusal text, matching Hermes' clear-only-on-boundary behavior.
Existing gateway reset, approval queue, and command policy tests remain green.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-09: TDD added internal/gateway.SlashConfirmationQueue with one pending confirmation per session, scoped supersede/clear semantics, once/always/cancel resolution, ID mismatch preservation, and no outcome on boundary clear. Gateway reset handling now clears only the target session's pending confirmation after ResetSession succeeds, while ErrResetDuringTurn preserves the confirmation and refusal text. Evidence: go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestSlashConfirm|TestManager_ResetClearsSlashConfirmation|TestManager_ResetDuringActiveTurnPreservesSlashConfirmation' -count=1; go test ./internal/gateway -count=1.
done_signal: Gateway fixtures prove slash confirmations are scoped, one-shot, fail-closed, and cleared only after a successful reset boundary.

item.name: Hermes live-turn prompt assembly parity (channel-neutral)
item.contract: Live gateway turns for every channel (Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, BlueBubbles, Discord, Sage Goblin, future) assemble a system-prompt header that mirrors Hermes' run_agent.py / prompt_builder.py block order before the user message: (1) SOUL.md identity, (2) tool/memory guidance, (3) USER.md / MEMORY.md durable user context, (4) skills guidance, (5) AGENTS.md / .hermes.md / project context, (6) timestamp + model + provider metadata, (7) platform/session context. Assembly happens once inside `gateway.Manager` at the existing `BuildSessionContextPrompt` call site so all channel adapters inherit it without channel-specific code. The umbrella tracks the seven-block contract; child rows deliver each block.
item.degraded_mode: Complete child rows now inject the channel-neutral live-turn prompt header before the user message. Missing SOUL.md, project context, USER.md, MEMORY.md, metadata seams, or self-help guidance gates still degrade by eliding only that block and preserving the platform/session block. Threat-pattern scans continue to block raw prompt-injection content before provider submission.
ready_when: internal/hermes/context_files.go BuildContextFilesPrompt is complete (it is) and exposes channel-neutral SOUL/project block rendering with threat-scan guards.
internal/gateway/manager.go owns a single channel-neutral assembly site (BuildSessionContextPrompt at line 1534) where the prepend can land for all channels at once.
Each child row carries its own ready_when independent of the others so SOUL/project block can ship without USER/MEMORY/skills/tools/timestamp blocks.
not_ready_when: The umbrella is selected as a single slice rather than executed through child rows.
Wiring is added inside any one channel adapter (internal/channels/telegram, internal/channels/slack, internal/channels/bluebubbles, etc.) instead of inside gateway.Manager.

A child row mutates BuildContextFilesPrompt instead of consuming it, or modifies kernel.PlatformEvent to add new system-prompt fields when the existing SessionContext field already carries the assembled header.
acceptance: internal/gateway/live_turn_prompt_test.go captures kernel/provider submits and proves the rendered system-prompt header includes SOUL/project context, USER.md/MEMORY.md durable context, timestamp/model/provider/session metadata, self-help guidance when gated, and platform/session context before the user message.
Channel-neutrality fixtures prove the assembled header path is shared across fake Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, BlueBubbles, and Discord channels.
A captured final provider request proves a Telegram-shaped turn carries Gormes identity and durable operator context as the leading system message before the user message.
item.note: Validated by the completed child rows for SOUL/project context, durable USER/MEMORY context, timestamp/model/provider/session metadata, self-help guidance, prompt-builder guidance constants, and production cmd/gormes metadata wiring. The stale planned umbrella has been reconciled so progress surfaces no longer advertise already-shipped live-turn prompt assembly as future work.
done_signal: Focused live-turn prompt tests, gateway/hermes/kernel package tests, progress validation, and full-suite validation have all passed with the umbrella complete.

provenance.note: Hermes assembles system-prompt blocks per turn inside the agent runtime; Gormes assembles them inside gateway.Manager so the channel-neutral TurnAdapter / kernel.PlatformEvent.SessionContext seam already in place is reused. No kernel.PlatformEvent shape change required.

item.name: Live-turn SOUL.md and project context wiring (channel-neutral)
item.contract: gateway.Manager invokes internal/hermes.BuildContextFilesPrompt once per inbound submit and prepends the rendered SOUL.md + project context block (HERMES.md / .hermes.md / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / .cursorrules per BuildContextFilesPrompt's existing first-match-wins precedence) to the existing BuildSessionContextPrompt block before the kernel.PlatformEvent.SessionContext field is set. The wiring lives inside gateway.Manager — never inside any channel adapter — so Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, BlueBubbles, Discord, Sage Goblin, and any future channel inherit the block automatically. Profile dir resolution uses config.GormesHome() in production with a fakeable seam for tests; CWD resolution uses the manager's configured working directory with a fakeable seam. ContextFilesReport evidence is logged via gateway telemetry but never sent on the channel.
item.degraded_mode: Missing SOUL.md or missing project context returns an empty block from BuildContextFilesPrompt — the existing platform/session block is injected unchanged and no error reaches the channel. A SOUL.md that trips the threat-pattern scan is rendered as the existing `[BLOCKED: ...]` marker and never reaches the provider as raw threat content. A truncated SOUL.md or AGENTS.md carries the existing `[...truncated ... kept H+T of N chars ...]` marker. A failed file read is logged via telemetry and the block is dropped for that turn.
ready_when: BuildContextFilesPrompt is complete and exposes channel-neutral SOUL + project rendering with threat-scan guards (verified — internal/hermes/context_files.go ships and is tested).
The single channel-neutral assembly site at gateway/manager.go:1534 is intact (verified — BuildSessionContextPrompt already lives there and feeds kernel.PlatformEvent.SessionContext).
Tests can construct a fake gateway turn with injected fakes for profile dir + CWD + channel; no live filesystem state under ~/.gormes or ~/.hermes is read.
not_ready_when: The slice modifies internal/hermes/context_files.go, internal/kernel/frame.go, internal/kernel/kernel.go, or any channel adapter under internal/channels/.
The slice ports USER.md, MEMORY.md, skills guidance, tool guidance, or time/model/provider metadata — those are sibling child rows.
The slice adds a channel name check (`if platform == 'telegram'`) anywhere on the assembly path.
The slice exposes raw absolute paths or raw threat content to the channel; only redacted evidence may be logged through telemetry.
The slice changes BuildSessionContextPrompt behavior or its byte output for the existing platform/session block.
acceptance: TestLiveTurn_SystemPrompt_IncludesSOUL: a fake gateway turn dispatched with a fake profile dir containing SOUL.md='You are Gormes, not ChatGPT.' produces a captured kernel.PlatformEvent.SessionContext that contains the exact substring 'You are Gormes, not ChatGPT.'.

TestLiveTurn_SystemPrompt_IncludesProjectContext: a fake gateway turn dispatched with a fake CWD containing AGENTS.md='Project: Gormes — native Go Hermes parity agent.' produces a captured kernel.PlatformEvent.SessionContext that contains the AGENTS.md body.

TestLiveTurn_SystemPrompt_BlockOrder: a fake gateway turn with both SOUL.md and AGENTS.md fixtures produces a captured SessionContext where the SOUL/project header precedes the existing BuildSessionContextPrompt platform/session block, which precedes any user-bound recall content. The recall ordering test from the existing kernel session_context_test fixture must continue to pass unchanged.

TestLiveTurn_SystemPrompt_ChannelNeutral: the same fake turn fixture run through fake Telegram, Slack, BlueBubbles, WhatsApp, and Discord channel adapters produces a byte-identical SOUL/project block in each captured kernel submit.

TestLiveTurn_SystemPrompt_MissingProfileNoPanic: a fake gateway turn with no SOUL.md and no project context produces a captured SessionContext byte-identical to the current (pre-wiring) BuildSessionContextPrompt-only output, proving the existing block is unchanged when context-files content is absent.

TestLiveTurn_SystemPrompt_ThreatBlocked: a fake gateway turn with a SOUL.md containing 'ignore previous instructions' produces a captured SessionContext whose SOUL block carries the `[BLOCKED:` marker and never carries the raw threat string.
item.note: Critical 2026-04-29 P0 fix: live Telegram evidence shows Gormes replying 'I'm ChatGPT.' to 'Whats ur name?' because the live provider request omits the Hermes identity stack. This slice flips the visible identity by wiring the already-shipped BuildContextFilesPrompt into the channel-neutral gateway.Manager assembly site. done_signal: Six named fixtures pass; gateway.Manager prepends the BuildContextFilesPrompt block at the existing BuildSessionContextPrompt site; no channel adapter under internal/channels/ is modified; restart smoke confirms Gormes identity through Telegram with the project's SOUL.md.

item.contract: Extend the completed platform reconnect/failed-queue seam (internal/gateway/platform_reconnect.go ReconnectFailedPlatforms / PlatformFailure) with Hermes' per-platform circuit breaker so the gateway keeps running when one platform keeps failing: after a configurable threshold of consecutive retryable failures (Hermes _PAUSE_AFTER_FAILURES=10) the platform is marked paused, kept in the failed set with a pause_reason and a far-future next_retry, surfaced as platform_state="paused" in the runtime status read-model, and skipped by the reconnect watcher until manually resumed. Add a gateway-only `/platform <pause|resume|list> [name]` operator slash command (the Go port of gateway/run.py:_handle_platform_command, registered in internal/gateway/commands.go CommandRegistry as gateway_only with args_hint "<pause|resume|list> [name]" like the existing handler ports) where: `/platform pause <name>` pauses a queued platform (idempotent; rejects an unqueued platform), `/platform resume <name>` unpauses, resets the attempt counter and schedules an immediate retry (returns a clear not-paused/not-queued message otherwise), `/platform list` shows connected and paused platforms, bare `/platform` prints usage plus the list, and an unknown platform name is rejected with guidance. Auto-pause must log/return the Hermes-shaped 'fix the issue then run `/platform resume <name>`' guidance. This row does not reopen the completed reconnect-isolation row and does not change provider retry behavior.

item.name: Gateway /model interactive provider/model picker

item.name: Multimodal photo attachment passthrough
item.contract: TurnAdapter.Dispatch materializes inbound gateway.Attachment{Kind:"photo"} entries into kernel.PlatformEvent.ContentParts as hermes.MessageContentPart{Type:"image_url", ImageURL:"data:<media-type>;base64,..."} before submitting to the kernel. Vision-capable providers (currently openai-codex/gpt-5.5 on the operator's PC, plus Anthropic, Codex Responses, OpenRouter/etc.) receive the image bytes directly through the existing provider stack. Non-photo attachments (voice, document) are skipped — voice has its own transcriber resolver and documents lack a defined multimodal contract today. Unreadable cache files are silently dropped so the existing text-marker fallback in SubmitText remains the user-visible signal and the kernel never sees a broken image_url.

Existing image_shrink_retry handles oversized payloads on retry without adapter-side bounds.

The implementation changes existing channel approval button payloads or callback authorization behavior.

item.name: Gateway mutating-subcommand unavailability stub
item.contract: Gateway lifecycle CLI provides local safe `stop` and `restart` commands over validated runtime PID evidence: stop interrupts only the validated live gateway, restart first tries a fakeable systemd user-service restart on Linux, then falls back to the validated runtime record by restarting a live managed gateway or starting a fresh gateway when no live managed runtime exists, while unsupported start/install/uninstall subcommands surface a stable `unavailable` error with a pointer to the existing internal/cli/service_restart.go helper instead of silently failing or shelling out through untested paths.
item.degraded_mode: `gormes gateway stop` is idempotent when runtime status is missing, stale, or pid-reused; it signals only a PID validated as the live Gormes gateway and refuses to stop while active_agents is non-zero. `gormes gateway restart` reports service-manager restart evidence when systemd succeeds, bounds service-manager restart calls with the requested timeout, falls back to the runtime record when the service manager is unavailable, starts a fresh gateway when the runtime record is missing or stale, and refuses active-agent or unsafe PID-validation restarts. Unsupported start/install/uninstall subcommands print a deterministic `gateway: <subcommand> is not available; use the systemd/service_restart helper` message and exit with a stable non-zero code.
ready_when: Gateway management CLI read-model closeout is complete (read-only baseline already landed).
internal/cli/service_restart.go provides the systemd/launchd helper that the unavailability message points to.
not_ready_when: The slice actually shells out to systemd/launchd/sc.exe in tests, or installs/uninstalls real services from a Go test process.
`gateway stop` signals a PID without validated live gateway runtime evidence.
The slice rewrites the existing `gateway status` subcommand or changes the runtime status read path.
acceptance: `gormes gateway stop` reads validated runtime status, sends an interrupt only to the validated live gateway PID when active_agents is zero, waits for status to become non-live, and reports the validation status used for the stop result.

`gormes gateway stop` exits successfully without signalling when runtime status is missing, stale, stopped, pid-reused, or otherwise not live; it returns an actionable error without signalling when active_agents is non-zero.

`gormes gateway restart` on Linux delegates to a fakeable systemd user-service manager when available, passes the requested timeout into the restart context, and emits JSON restart evidence after active-status polling reports restarted.

`gormes gateway restart` falls back to the recorded live runtime when the service manager is unavailable: it writes planned-stop evidence, interrupts the validated live PID, starts a detached gateway process, waits for a new live PID, and refuses restarts while active_agents is non-zero.

`gormes gateway restart` starts a detached gateway instead of erroring when validated runtime status proves no live managed process exists; it does not signal stale, missing, pid-reused, or permission-denied PIDs.

Adding unsupported mutating subcommands `start`, `install`, and `uninstall` to gatewayCmd registers a deterministic unavailability handler that returns `gateway: <subcommand> is not available; use the service_restart helper` and exits non-zero.

Tests in cmd/gormes/gateway_mutating_unavailable_test.go invoke `gormes gateway stop`, `gormes gateway restart`, and every unsupported mutating verb, asserting signal/no-signal behavior, service-manager timeout context evidence, runtime restart/start evidence, or unavailable error + non-zero exit code without requiring live systemd/launchd.
The existing `gateway status` subcommand and runtime status path are unchanged.
No new persistent gateway runtime state file is introduced; service-manager access remains behind fakeable seams and unit tests do not shell out to live service managers.
item.note: Split out of `Gateway management CLI read-model closeout` 2026-04-26 and closed the same day. cmd/gormes/gateway.go originally registered start/stop/restart/install/uninstall as deterministic unavailability stubs (gatewayMutatingUnavailableSubcommands + newGatewayMutatingUnavailableCommand) returning `gateway: <subcommand> is not available; use the service_restart helper` with stable exit code 2 via newExitCodeError; cmd/gormes/gateway_mutating_unavailable_test.go covered each verb, asserted no runtime/state file is opened, and verified `gateway status` is unaffected. 2026-04-30 dev-loop hardening promotes `gateway stop` from unavailable stub to safe local stop: cmd/gormes/gateway_stop.go reads validated runtime status, signals only the live gateway PID with os.Interrupt, waits for non-live validation, and treats missing/stale runtime as idempotent no-op so bin/gormes and go-run gateway testing can release sessions.db without killing by process name. 2026-05-14 lifecycle follow-up promotes non-Windows `gateway restart` from unavailable stub to a fakeable service-manager/runtime restart command while keeping start/install/uninstall on the deterministic unavailable path. 2026-05-15 hardening makes service-manager restart calls honor the requested timeout context and makes runtime fallback start a fresh detached gateway when no live managed runtime exists instead of failing the operator-facing restart command.

item.name: Gormes update bundled assets and skills sync
item.contract: After release binary update is safe, release-installed `gormes update` must read a verified release manifest and apply only manifest-enumerated bundled assets and bundled skills. The manifest is part of the trusted release chain: strict schema, path, digest, and duplicate-entry validation must complete before mutation; local web builds and runtime directory scans are not authoritative for release installs. Update snapshots every file it may mutate, updates all known profiles with digest-based three-way bundled skill sync, preserves user-modified active skills, writes deterministic conflict copies for new bundled versions, removes only unmodified removed-from-manifest bundled skills, marks modified removed skills as orphaned, records a release install ledger/report, and supports rollback of update-mutated files with post-update-edit conflict preservation. User config, credentials, sessions, memory databases, operator-created files, service drain/restart behavior, and public component-selection flags are out of scope for this slice.
item.degraded_mode: Missing or invalid release manifest, asset checksum mismatch, unwritable asset directory, skill conflict, or rollback failure emits typed evidence and preserves user-modified content; update may finish with a degraded sync report only when the binary remains valid and user state was not clobbered.

A release-installed update applies only manifest-enumerated assets/skills and does not run local web builds or scan arbitrary bundled directories as authority.

item.name: Gateway stale-code self-check uses git HEAD SHA
item.contract: Gormes gateway stale-code detection compares the gateway boot commit against the current git HEAD SHA instead of source-file mtimes, so agent edits to tracked files do not trigger stale-code restart guidance while a real git pull/checkout that advances HEAD still does.
item.degraded_mode: Non-git installs, unreadable git metadata, missing packed refs, or disappearing worktrees return stale_code_git_unavailable evidence and skip restart advice instead of crashing or falling back to mtime false positives.
ready_when: Runtime status JSON + PID/process validation and gateway status read-model rows are complete.
Tests can create temp git metadata fixtures for normal checkouts, worktrees, packed refs, detached HEAD, and non-git installs without invoking git subprocesses or running a gateway process.
not_ready_when: The slice edits service start/stop semantics, planned-stop markers, auto-update behavior, or source-file watcher behavior unrelated to stale-code classification.
The helper shells out to git during status checks or treats arbitrary file mtime changes as stale code.
acceptance: Boot SHA equal to current HEAD reports not stale even when a tracked source file mtime changes after boot.
Current HEAD changing to a different SHA reports stale code and includes redacted restart guidance evidence.
Fixtures cover normal `.git` directories, worktree `.git` files with commondir, packed refs, and detached HEAD.
Non-git or unreadable git metadata reports unavailable/no-stale evidence and does not panic.
Repeated checks use the bounded cache without hiding a later HEAD change beyond the configured freshness window.
done_signal: Gateway stale-code fixtures prove HEAD-SHA comparison handles source edits, real HEAD changes, worktrees, packed refs, detached HEAD, cache bounds, and non-git installs without git subprocesses.

provenance.note: 2026-05-06 all-topic parity sweep raised this install/runtime row to P1 because the existing P1 planned rows were blocked, broad, or not actually builder-ready, while Hermes' active gateway self-check now keys stale-code advice to git HEAD SHA instead of source mtimes. item.name: TUI gateway completion path normalizer

TestNormalizeCompletionPath_NoExpansionOnWindows leaves C:/Users/x as C:/Users/x when isWindows=true.

item.name: Gateway outbound sends publish message-sent events
item.contract: Gateway manager successful outbound sends publish channel-neutral gateway.message.sent events through an injected EventDispatcher. Existing channel Send/SendReply delivery remains the source of truth; the bus event is post-delivery provenance for TUI, dashboard, audit, and future outbound subscribers, and event publication must not block user-visible sends.
item.degraded_mode: If the EventDispatcher is nil, unavailable, or fails to publish, the channel send remains successful and the manager records only local debug evidence; no second event bus is started.
ready_when: Event bus core and EventDispatcher PublishMessageSent are complete and validated.
Manager send hooks already wrap successful Send and SendReply delivery through HookAfterSend, so the slice can add a post-delivery event producer without changing channel SDK adapters.
not_ready_when: The slice rewrites channel delivery, coalescer editing, Telegram thread fallback, or the kernel turn loop.
Event publication happens before a channel send succeeds, blocks a successful user-visible send, or reclassifies send failures as successful message-sent events.
Tests require live Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, WeCom, Weixin, provider credentials, or a running gateway process.
acceptance: Manager fixtures prove a successful outbound send publishes exactly one gateway.message.sent event with source/platform, chat_id, message_id/msg_id, kind, text/body, and a non-empty trace_id.
Reply fixtures prove ReplyToMessageID is preserved when SendReply is used.
Failure fixtures prove channel send errors do not publish message-sent events and nil or failing dispatchers do not block successful sends.
Existing hook lifecycle and event dispatcher fixtures remain green.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-07: the bounded all-topic weakness sweep covered CLI/TUI, provider/auth, gateway/channels, tools, sessions/memory/Goncho, install/runtime, browser automation, docs/public surfaces, and release/operator flows. The event-bus parent had complete inbound channel adapters and a synthetic full-flow proof but no manager-side outbound delivery producer. TDD added an optional ManagerConfig.EventDispatcher and post-success HookAfterSend publisher so successful Send/SendReply delivery emits exactly one gateway.message.sent event with platform/source, chat_id, sent message_id/msg_id, kind, text/body, reply_to_message_id when applicable, and a stable trace_id. Send failures do not publish message-sent events, and nil or failing dispatchers do not block successful visible sends.
done_signal: Gateway manager send fixtures prove post-delivery gateway.message.sent events are emitted with provenance, reply context, and degraded no-block behavior.

item.name: Delta-bounded skill and memory maintenance passes
item.contract: Learning-loop maintenance accepts changed source IDs, per-source sync-anchor evidence, and stale semantic-refresh hints so skill/memory extraction, scoring, and embedding refresh can no-op or process only changed records instead of rescanning the whole local corpus
item.degraded_mode: Maintenance status reports delta_noop, delta_sources_missing, source_anchor_missing, source_anchor_global_fallback, stale_refresh_empty, or full_scan_fallback evidence instead of silently doing whole-corpus work.
ready_when: The row is an evidence-only maintenance planner: it can run before retrieval scoring because it does not change skill selection, prompt injection, or memory recall.
The worker can use fake skill/memory rows plus injected source-anchor and stale-count callbacks; no live embeddings, Ollama, Postgres/PGLite, git cat-file, or tree-sitter runtime is required.
not_ready_when: The slice requires live embedding calls or reads the whole checkout/memory corpus in unit tests.
The slice changes prompt injection or skill selection behavior before the maintenance evidence shape is fixture-locked.
acceptance: TestDeltaMaintenance_NoChangedSourcesReturnsNoop passes an empty changed-source list and asserts no extractor/scorer/embedding callback is invoked and status evidence is delta_noop.
TestDeltaMaintenance_ProcessesOnlyChangedSources passes two changed skill or memory source IDs and asserts only those IDs reach the fake extractor/scorer.
TestDeltaMaintenance_SourceAnchorEvidence passes a matching source ID plus source-scoped last_commit and asserts the plan records source_anchor=per_source instead of global fallback.
TestDeltaMaintenance_GlobalAnchorFallbackIsExplicit omits source-anchor evidence and asserts the returned plan reports source_anchor_global_fallback before any broad scan is allowed.
TestDeltaMaintenance_StaleRefreshSkipsWhenCountZero injects staleCount=0 and asserts no stale text loader or embed callback runs.
TestDeltaMaintenance_FullScanFallbackIsExplicit omits changed-source evidence and asserts the returned plan marks full_scan_fallback instead of hiding a whole-corpus scan.
item.note: Complete 2026-04-30: TDD added a pure internal/skills delta-maintenance planner that accepts changed skill/memory source IDs, records per-source/global/missing anchor evidence, invokes extractor/scorer callbacks only for changed sources, skips stale loaders/embedders when staleCount=0, and returns explicit full_scan_fallback evidence when changed-source evidence is absent. Gormes-owned. Gormes-owned.22.5 added the follow-on sourceId cycle-sync fix so a per-source last_commit anchor prevents garbage-collected global anchors from forcing a full reimport. Gormes preserves those lessons as operator-visible maintenance evidence without importing Gormes-owned runtime.
done_signal: Delta maintenance fixtures prove no-op, changed-source-only, source-anchor evidence, stale-count-zero, and explicit full-scan fallback behavior with operator-visible evidence and no live embedding/runtime imports.

provenance.note: Gormes-owned provides the delta/stale/source-anchor maintenance lessons; Gormes adapts them to local skills and memory maintenance evidence without importing external database runtime.
